global_issues.title: US-Iran Deal Hopes Send Oil Plunging, Equities Rallying
global_issues.note: Confirmed by multiple outlets (The National, CNBC, Axios) — oil fell on Aug 3-4, 2026 on optimism for a Strait of Hormuz reopening deal after Trump paused a planned strike on Iran, with talks reportedly resuming Monday. WTI fell ~5.7% (briefing's '5%' is a slight rounding but directionally correct). Note: one source shows Brent actually rising ~5% same day, a divergence not mentioned in the briefing but not material to the core claim. The Strait itself reportedly remains largely closed despite the deal optimism — briefing doesn't caveat this, a minor omission.

missing_major_news.title: Jeff Bezos filed Form 144 to sell ~15 million AMZN shares (~$4.07B)
missing_major_news.impact: Directly explains AMZN's decline (-2.32% close) — the briefing's watchlist entry for AMZN cites no cause, and this insider-sale headline is a materially relevant, specific driver missing from context.

missing_major_news.title: AMD Q2 2026 earnings beat (EPS $1.66 vs $1.55 est, record Data Center revenue) but stock fell >8% on the report
missing_major_news.impact: AMD isn't in the watchlist directly, but it's a bellwether for the AI/semiconductor rotation narrative the briefing builds (CRWD, ANET framed as AI infra leaders) — a big post-earnings semiconductor selloff is relevant context that's absent.

market_mood_check.note: Dow closing above 54,000, S&P 500 record close, and PLTR's ~29% surge on its earnings beat (EPS $0.41 vs $0.33 est, revenue $1.94B vs $1.80B est) are all independently confirmed by CNBC/CNN coverage of Aug 4, 2026 trading.

sector_check.note: CRWD's accumulation/leadership framing is well supported (3-day rally, multiple analyst price-target hikes, sold-out Fal.Con conference). However, attributing VST (Vistra) and CEG (Constellation Energy) laggard status to 'oil price collapse reduces profitability' is a weak causal link — these are power-generation/nuclear utilities primarily driven by AI-datacenter electricity demand, not crude oil economics. The rationale conflates energy-sector oil exposure with power-generation stocks that have a different demand driver.

stock_errors.error: Briefing reports TSM closed at $417.17 (+2.72%); independent lookup for Aug 4, 2026 shows TSM trading/closing around $406.11, an ~2.7% discrepancy. Could not fully reconcile — flagging for review rather than confirming as definite error.

grok_report.summary: The briefing's core narrative (Iran/Hormuz deal optimism, oil plunge, record-setting equity rally, PLTR's earnings-driven surge, CRWD sector leadership) is well corroborated by independent sources. Weaknesses: it omits the Bezos insider-sale story that actually explains AMZN's decline, misattributes VST/CEG weakness to oil rather than power-demand dynamics, and has one unresolved price discrepancy on TSM.
